problem: LLM-based navigation converts global memory (semantic/topological maps) into text, losing geometric information, while VLM-based methods that only see the egocentric view (e.g. PIVOT) face partial observability and redundant exploration in long-horizon tasks.
motivation: Long-horizon ObjectNav in complex indoor spaces needs both global context (where the agent has been and what it has seen) and precise spatial grounding. The paper projects global memory cues directly onto the egocentric image so that the VLM can reason over both at once.
key_idea: Maintain a frontier map, landmark semantic memory and visitation memory, project frontier candidates and visited positions as numbered markers onto a panoramic egocentric image, and add LLM-retrieved top-k landmark descriptions (with distances) so the VLM picks the next marker.
insight: Global cues become usable when they are rendered in the ego-view (markers and blue visited circles) and supplemented by text-retrieved landmarks for targets that are out of view. Ablations show that removing landmark memory (HSSD SR 0.8685→0.8356) or visitation memory (→0.8450) each hurts. SFT of Llama3.2-11B on 30k GPT-4o-rationale VQA samples beats GPT-4o (HSSD SR 0.8732 vs 0.8685), and the gains are largest on HSSD-Hard.
method: Frontier map: an ESC-style voxel/occupancy map from RGB-D and pose; frontier centroids are clustered and snapped to the nearest floor grid point to give reachable candidate goals.

Panoramic observation: 4 RGB-D views at 90° steps are concatenated into a 360° panorama; candidates are projected with camera intrinsics and extrinsics and drawn as numbered green circles, and visited positions as blue circles.

Landmark semantic memory: the VLM describes the surroundings of each marker; descriptions are stored with global coordinates. An LLM retrieves the top-k task-relevant landmarks (numbered, with distance to the agent) for use when no visible marker is suitable.
Visitation memory: records past positions, shown as blue markers that the VLM is told to avoid, reducing redundant exploration.

Memory-augmented decision making: a CoT prompt makes the VLM output a thought and one marker ID; the marker is converted to global coordinates and executed with Habitat's shortest path follower. Memory is then updated.

SFT data pipeline: 40 new HSSD object categories, A* trajectories smoothed with Bézier curves, and GPT-4o dual-phase rationale generation plus verification. This yields 30,352 VQA pairs (marker description and marker selection) from 104 scenes and 5,678 tasks, used to fine-tune Llama3.2-11B-Vision (3 epochs, lr 1e-5, batch size 128).

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen) as the main model; Llama3.2-11B-Vision (vanilla and SFT) as variants
setting.model_size: Llama3.2-11B (the GPT-4o variant is a closed API)
setting.training_data: None for the GPT-4o variant (zero-shot). The SFT variant uses 30,352 VQA pairs (marker description + selection with rationale) generated with GPT-4o from 104 HSSD scenes / 5,678 tasks over 40 object categories.
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB-D with pose (4 views at 90° forming a panorama)
setting.action_space: Habitat discrete actions (STOP, FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN ±30°), with the VLM selecting a waypoint marker executed by the shortest-path follower
setting.simulator: Habitat 3.0 (HSSD, HM3D) plus a real mobile robot
setting.privileged: Habitat ground-truth semantic segmentation (with object size conditions) is used as the perception module in simulation; the shortest-path follower uses the navmesh.

numbers_note: Metrics are reported as fractions (0-1) in the paper and copied as printed. The HM3D baselines are taken from the original papers, except PIVOT. The real-robot result is reported only as a figure and text (26.51 m / 630° vs 33.88 m / 810° for w/o landmark memory; PIVOT failed).
results: With GPT-4o, Mem2Ego reaches SR 0.8685 / SPL 0.5788 on HSSD, beating the strongest baseline PIVOT (0.7840 / 0.5658). On HSSD-Hard its SR is 0.7647, 12.75% higher than PIVOT (0.6372), and on HM3D it reaches SR 0.766 / SPL 0.441, above VLFM (0.636 / 0.325). SFT Llama3.2-11B surpasses GPT-4o (0.8732 SR on HSSD, 0.7843 SR on HSSD-Hard).
limitations: Landmark memory relies on the VLM's text descriptions of markers, which may lose semantic information; egocentric images are not stored in memory.
Failures come mainly from hitting the step limit and from VLM hallucination, such as selecting markers that do not exist.
Simulation uses GT semantic segmentation as perception, and the evaluation subsets are small (213 and 102 episodes).
